title: Hordes on the State Map
summary: Hordes are crowds of the dead that move as one token across the State Map: hives build them and give each a job (guard, build, roam, attack, border); they merge, split, follow noise and fall on bases.
whyHere: First card of the dead milestone: the per-tile dead population is static pressure, hordes make it move. They carry the hives' armies (96) and are what walls and sieges (99, 100) answer.
sliceScope: Border hordes only: every 5–9 days a horde of 10–25 enters on a border tile, roams up to 2 tiles a day toward the noisiest base it can reach, merges with another it meets; at a base it calls a stub hold check (def.walls replaces it) and raises a warning card when a lookout sees it.
fullScope: Sizes small 10–25 / medium 50–80 / large 100–200 (hive cost 3/8/15), score ~3/8/16. At most 2 tiles a day (12 h a tile, slower in snow and deep cold; frozen rivers crossable). Carries a special-dead mix through merges, splits only if each part keeps 10+. Attacks bases up to 45 tiles away, yours weighted 2.5× a group's; generators and shelter heat draw them, silent running hides you.

data: hordes.json: size table (min, max, cost) and per-role rules (speed, wander radius, merges with)
Noise source weights (generator, gunfire, base size, silent running)
Border spawn config (interval 5–9 days, size odds by game day)
Horde terrain cost table for the hex pather (river, snow, mountain)
backend: Horde record + HordeSystem.DailyTick: accumulate progress hours, step along an A* hex path (travel.pathing) with horde costs
Merge (same tile, compatible role: counts add, mix weighted by count) and Split (each part ≥10)
TargetScorer.Score(horde, base): one function for every base, player or group (ADR 0001); the 2.5× player weight is a data value, not an if
On arrival publish HordeArrivedAtBase(baseId, hordeId); on sighting HordeSighted → warning card
Unit tests: merge conserves count & mix, split floor, same seed → same positions after 60 days
ui: Horde token on the State Map: crowd icon, count label, drift arrow
Tile panel row 'A horde of ~60 (runners)'
Warning card: 'The dead are coming' with ETA

connections.why: Hives spend resources on hordes and receive 'build' hordes at new sites.
connections.how: HiveSystem calls HordeFactory.Spawn(hiveId, sizeKey, role, mix); a build horde reaching its site calls HiveSites.Deliver(siteId, horde.Score).
connections.godot: SimHost turns HordeSpawned / HordeRemoved events into signals the HordeLayer node listens to.
connections.unity: SimHost raises C# events HordeSpawned / HordeRemoved; a HordeLayer MonoBehaviour subscribes in OnEnable.

connections.why: A horde at a base is beaten at the walls or breaks in.
connections.how: HordeArrivedAtBase event → DefenceResolver.HoldCheck(base, horde), the same call for player and group bases.
connections.godot: Signal opens the warning / deploy dialog when the base is yours.
connections.unity: UnityEvent on SimHost opens the deploy panel when the base is yours.

connections.why: Players must see hordes drift and judge their size.
connections.how: Read-only HordeView DTOs (id, tile, count, heading) built after each tick; the view never touches Horde objects.
connections.godot: HordeLayer (Node2D) keeps Dictionary<int, HordeToken>; tweens a token to the new hex centre with Tween.
connections.unity: Pooled token prefabs (ObjectPool) keyed by horde id; lerp positions in Update between ticks.

connections.why: Autopilot and AI groups flee, cull or prepare for hordes.
connections.how: Governor reads hordes through its KnowledgeMap (only seen/reported ones), never the true list.
connections.godot: No engine code: sim-to-sim.
connections.unity: No engine code: sim-to-sim.

godot.approach: Hordes are pure sim data; Godot only draws them. A HordeLayer Node2D under the State Map owns one token per horde, moved by Tween between hex centres (hex→pixel from core.hexgrid) when SimHost signals HordeMoved. For the 'shuffling crowd' draw 5–30 small figures jittered in a circle sized by count, cheaply with a MultiMeshInstance2D.

unity.approach: A HordeLayer MonoBehaviour pools token prefabs (SpriteRenderer + TextMeshPro count) keyed by horde id and lerps them in Update. For big crowds draw the figures with Graphics.RenderMeshInstanced instead of hundreds of GameObjects. Use a sorting layer so hordes sit above terrain and below UI.

learn.t: Red Blob Games: Introduction to A* (BFS, flood fill)

newb: A horde is ONE record with a count, not 200 agents. Aggregating like this is 'level of detail' for simulation: thousands of dead cost almost nothing on the strategic map.
Movement as 'progress hours' toward the next tile (the same pattern as parties) keeps it deterministic and frame-rate independent.
The view interpolates; the sim jumps tile to tile once per tick. Never let the visual position feed back into the rules.
Merging needs a weighted average for the mix (60 dead with 10% runners + 40 with none = 6% runners).
pitfalls: Simulating every zombie individually on the State Map
Player-only targeting code: one scoring function for every base keeps AI parity
Using UnityEngine.Random / GD.Randf in sim code instead of the seeded Rng
Pathing every horde every hour; plan a path once and re-plan only when blocked or retargeted
test: xUnit: spawn and move N days = expected tiles along the path; merge sums counts and weights mix; split refuses parts under 10; 60-day run is identical for the same seed; a noisier nearer base wins targeting for player and group alike. Manual: headless 1-year census (like tools/hordecensus.js) and watch hordes drift to bases on a dev overlay.

title: Hives, hive birth & hive tech tree
summary: Hives are the dead's nests: they earn resources daily, keep a guard horde, spend on hordes and on a tech tree of 'growths' that unlock special dead, found new hives through gatherings you can see and break up, and every one must be destroyed to win.
whyHere: Needs hordes to spend on. It is the main win condition (meta.victory) and the engine behind special dead (97), the hive crawl (98) and the counter-dead that read your defences.
sliceScope: 2–3 hives, income 1 a day (+cluster bonus), each funds its guard horde first, then roaming/attack hordes; one growth (biomass pit, +1 income); destroying a hive (stub: beat its guard by auto-resolve until 98 lands) removes it and runs the victory check.
fullScope: A Normal map starts with 5–6 hives (5 at the outbreak origin, 3 per extra hot spot by world size), 5 resources each. Income alone 1/day, two within 5 tiles 3 each, three 6 each, +2 per further hive up to 12. ~25 growths in tiers 0–4 (biomass pit 12 for 10 days … mutation vat 60 for 60) within 2 tiles, burnable and regrowing; Wallbreaker 40 (den, from day 200, 1 per 90 days). New sites: ~a year to the first, then every 4–5 months, 5–8 in three years on big maps; a mass of 1,000 dead at ≤40 a day (~4 weeks). Holds 4 tiles.

data: growths.json: id, tier, cost, days, max, unlocks (kind id), income/incomeMult, guard bonus, danger, artKey
hives.json: income-by-cluster table, horde costs, Wallbreaker rules, tier by game day & hive age
Site curve: first-site day, gap, NEW_CAP by world size, mass size, daily mass rate
Rumour / known rules (radio coverage, base and team distances)
backend: HiveSystem.Daily: income → fund guard → GrowthWish → buy hordes / growths; hives roll their own Rng stream
GrowthWish as a small scorer: income while young/poor, brood chamber after an attack, kinds cluster-mates lack, save up to N days
HiveSites: pick site, hordes within 10 tiles deliver, mass converts ≤40/day, hive stands at 1,000
HiveBirth watch: rumour, 'dead massing' card, Cull / Break up (setback, pause) via knowledge rules
Destroy(hiveId): wither growths, fade infection, publish HiveDestroyed; VictoryCheck needs no hive AND no site under way
Census test: 3 sim years on Large over 3 seeds stays within NEW_CAP
ui: Hive and growth icons with tooltips (what it gives)
Build-site mound with 'stands in ~N days' or '?' when stale
'The dead are massing near X' card: Break it up / Mark / Ignore

connections.why: Hordes are what hives buy; build hordes feed new sites.
connections.how: HordeFactory.Spawn(...) from HiveSystem.Buy; HiveSites.Deliver(siteId, score) from the horde's arrival.
connections.godot: No engine code: sim-to-sim.
connections.unity: No engine code: sim-to-sim.

connections.why: Growths unlock the kinds a hive's hordes carry.
connections.how: Hive.UnlockedKinds() feeds HordeMix.Build(hive, rng); counter growths gated by hive.Adapt.
connections.godot: Codex and tooltips read GrowthDef/ZombieTypeDef from ContentDb.
connections.unity: Codex and tooltips read the same ContentDb records.

connections.why: A hive is destroyed by killing its Hivemind at the end of the crawl.
connections.how: HivemindKilled(hiveId) event → HiveSystem.Destroy(hiveId); the crawl's brood is built from the guard horde.
connections.godot: SimHost signal returns from the crawl scene to the State Map with a result card.
connections.unity: SimHost C# event unloads the crawl scene and shows the result card.

connections.why: Destroying every hive is a victory.
connections.how: HiveDestroyed → VictoryCheck.Evaluate(world); no hive and no site under way = win.
connections.godot: Signal opens the victory screen with 'Keep playing'.
connections.unity: Event opens the victory panel with 'Keep playing'.

connections.why: Hives attack group bases and groups fight nearby hives (parity).
connections.how: AttackTarget scoring covers every Base; group governors get a 'hive war' option weighted by type.
connections.godot: No engine code: sim-to-sim.
connections.unity: No engine code: sim-to-sim.

godot.approach: Hive land and the red-skull ring go on an overlay TileMapLayer; hives and growths are Sprite2D markers looked up by art key. The massing card is a ui.cards dialog. Build an infra.devtools panel listing each hive's resources, tier and current wish: you will tune this system for weeks.

unity.approach: An overlay Tilemap paints hive land; growth markers are prefabs whose sprite comes from the ArtCatalog ScriptableObject by art key. Tooltips and the massing card in UI Toolkit. Same dev panel idea for tuning.

newb: A tech tree is just data: nodes with a cost, a tier (prerequisite) and effects. The 'AI' choosing a node is a scorer over the affordable ones.
Treat hives as a rival economy: income in, purchases out. Making that economy visible (rumours, mounds, growths) is what makes them feel fair.
Give hives their own Rng stream: then tweaking hive numbers doesn't reshuffle every other random event in a seed.
You will balance this with headless runs (years in seconds), not by playing: plan for a census tool early.
pitfalls: Growth effects hard-coded as if-chains per id instead of effect fields
Unbounded hive spread on big maps: cap with a curve per world size
Victory check forgetting a hive still being born
Forgetting to wither a destroyed hive's growths (they keep unlocking kinds)
test: xUnit: income table values; guard funded before hordes; a growth deducts its cost and completes after its days; new-site cadence within cap over 1,095 days on Large for 3 seeds; Destroy withers growths and the last one wins. Manual: 3-year headless run with the hive dev panel.

title: Special dead, counter-dead, bosses & tunnels
summary: The dead beyond walkers and runners: brutes, spitters, screamers, crawlers, carriers and worm swarms, dead beasts and more; the counter-dead a hive breeds against the defences it meets (Digger, Melter, Husk, Tripper, Dark-walker); bosses on 2×2 cells; and Digger tunnels that stay on your base map until filled.
whyHere: Needs hives (who breed them) and the tactical systems (combat.ai, combat.los, combat.stealth). It sits just before def.walls because the counter-dead read and cut those defences.
sliceScope: Data-driven kinds brute, spitter, screamer and crawler, each with one behaviour hook, placed in battles from a horde's mix; grid occupancy that supports a 2×2 Broodmother.
fullScope: ~25 kinds. Runner 6 tiles an action; brute 2.4× hp, takes ¾, hits 1.5×, smashes cover; spitter acid every other turn; screamer calls 1–2 more (6 a battle max); crawler unseen beyond 2.5 tiles unless lit, first bite 1.4×. Counter-dead at most 12% a kind, 20% together, the hive paying 0.25–0.5 each. Digger tunnels up to 8 cells, 3 cells a turn, each open one −8% hold (max 40%), filling 4 + 2 work-hours a cell. From day 60 the pool widens by place and era.

data: zombietypes.json: hp, dmg, aim, mob, armor, share, wall, breedCost, behaviour key, size (1 or 2), counters, artKey
Counter table: kind → defence part (walls, trench, wire, mines, light) and its cut
Dig constants (range, per turn, gain, crawl cost, fill hours)
Era pool: place × year → extra kinds and shares
backend: IZombieBehaviour per behaviour key (Brute.Smash, Spitter.Spit, Screamer.Call, Crawler.Hide, Digger.Dig…) run by combat.ai before the default chase
Footprint-aware occupancy: a 2×2 unit answers UnitAt on all four cells, range by nearest cell
DefenceProfile(base) → 0–1 per part for ANY base; hive.Adapt drifts toward it daily and jumps on contact; CounterMix with caps
Tunnels: dig when the flow field gains ≥4 moves; unit off-map while digging; link ends in combat pathing; persist on Base.Tunnels; FillTunnel construction job
Per-kind unit tests with a fixed Rng
ui: Placeholder silhouette + letter + colour per kind
Codex row 'what counters it'
Tunnel hole marker on the base map, click → Fill
Log: 'The hive near X has begun breeding Diggers'

connections.how: BehaviourRegistry[def.Behaviour].TryAct(battle, unit, rng) runs first; false falls back to the default dead brain.
connections.godot: SimHost forwards UnitAbility(unitId, "shriek") as a signal → AnimationPlayer / GPUParticles2D.
connections.unity: SimHost event → Animator.SetTrigger and a ParticleSystem burst.

connections.why: Counter-dead cut the hold of the defences they answer.
connections.how: DefenceResolver asks CounterDead.Cut(horde.Mix, base) and Tunnels.HoldCut(base); hives read DefenceProfile(base).
connections.godot: Deploy screen lists the counter-dead icons in the incoming horde.
connections.unity: Deploy panel lists the counter-dead icons in the incoming horde.

connections.why: Open tunnels stay on the base until filled.
connections.how: Base.Tunnels list; QueueFillTunnel(baseId, tunnelId) command adds a construction job.
connections.godot: Tunnel holes drawn on a TileMapLayer; a click sends QueueFillTunnel.
connections.unity: Tunnel tiles on a Tilemap; a click (WorldToCell) sends QueueFillTunnel.

connections.why: Tunnels and 2×2 bodies change movement.
connections.how: Pathing graph gets extra tunnel edges (cost 1.5 a cell) for units allowed to crawl; footprint check for big units.
connections.godot: No engine code: the sim paths.
connections.unity: No engine code: the sim paths.

godot.approach: One Unit scene for every kind, sized by the def (a 2×2 boss's sprite is anchored to its footprint centre). Abilities come from sim events and only trigger visuals (AnimationPlayer, GPUParticles2D for acid and shriek rings). A hidden crawler is simply not drawn until the sim says it is revealed: never compute visibility on the engine side.

unity.approach: A unit prefab whose sprite/animator comes from the ArtCatalog by art key; sim events set Animator triggers and fire Particle System bursts. 2D lights (URP) can show floodlit ground for the Dark-walker. Visibility stays in the sim.

learn.t: Red Blob Games: flow-field pathfinding (tower defense)

newb: Stats in JSON, behaviour as small classes picked by a key (the Strategy pattern): a new kind is a JSON row plus, at most, one class. Avoid a deep Zombie → Brute → EliteBrute inheritance tree.
Adaptation is a feedback loop: the hive reads what you built and breeds against it. Show the read to the player so it feels clever, not unfair.
'One unit per cell' is an assumption that breaks with 2×2 bosses: design occupancy as a footprint from the start.
A tunnel is just an extra edge in the pathfinding graph between two cells.
pitfalls: Special-casing player bases in DefenceProfile (parity: read any base by one rule)
Counter shares stacking into unbeatable hordes (keep the 12% / 20% caps)
Tunnel exits onto occupied, mined or unwalkable cells
Visual-only effects driving rules (e.g. particle collision deciding acid damage)
test: xUnit: screamer calls cap at 6; crawler unseen beyond 2.5 tiles unless lit; brute smashes cover only with no target; boss occupies 4 cells and is shot at its nearest cell; defence read moves toward a walled base; counter caps hold; Digger digs only when gain ≥4. Manual: dev command spawns each kind in a test battle.

title: The hive crawl
summary: Destroying a hive is a crawl through its den chamber by chamber: a round grid of T-shaped chambers with four mouths, read by warmth, drafts and the Hivemind's beat, down to the core where the Broodmother guards the Hivemind.
whyHere: Needs hives, the special dead and 2×2 bosses, plus deep tactics (interiors, stealth). It is the mid-to-late game's set piece and the real way to the hive victory.
sliceScope: A 2-ring den (a young hive) from the hive's seed, chambers fought on small maps from 3 templates, brood growing with depth, a core with Broodmother and Hivemind; kill the Hivemind → hive destroyed; leave by the mouth you came in.
fullScope: Depth by hive tier 2/3/5/7/9 rings (+1 with a screamer spire). Each chamber open on 3 sides with 1 wall, four mouths (N/E/S/W), the core open on 1–2 sides. Kinds: tunnels, galleries, nurseries, egg chambers, bone pits, worm pools, growth roots, collapses. Listening: (Scouting + Stealth) / 2 + d10 vs DC + perLayer × layer; 3 over exact, 0 rough, −4 a fumble that alerts. The den is the same every visit (seeded), regrown when the tier deepens it.

data: Chamber kinds: battle template ids, brood multiplier, loot
Depth by tier table and spire bonus
Listen DC table (base, per layer, thresholds)
Brood scaling by depth and the hive's guard
backend: DenGenerator.Build(hive, seed) deterministic: rings, one wall per chamber, four mouths, core in the inner rings
CrawlSession state machine: PickMouth → AtChamber → Listening → Fighting → Between → Leaving / Done
Listen check + odds by enumerating the d10's faces (the prototype once showed 50% for a real 60%)
Brood builder from the guard horde, mix and era kinds; carry wounds and ammo between chambers
Test: every mouth reaches the core (BFS) over 1,000 seeds
ui: Den map screen: rings of chambers, known/cleared marks, warmth and beat hints
Passage panel: Listen (with odds) / Go / Leave
Reuse the battle view for each chamber

connections.how: BattleSetup.FromChamber(chamber, brood) returns a BattleMap; the result returns to CrawlSession.
connections.godot: SimHost swaps the den-map Control for the Battle scene (SceneTree.ChangeSceneToFile or a child swap) and back.
connections.unity: SceneManager.LoadScene("Battle", Additive) per chamber, unloaded on result.

connections.why: The brood comes from the hive; the Hivemind's death destroys it.
connections.how: Brood from Hive.GuardHordeId; HivemindKilled(hiveId) → HiveSystem.Destroy.
connections.godot: Result card signal back on the State Map.
connections.unity: Result card event back on the State Map.

connections.why: A crawl can be saved halfway.
connections.how: CrawlSession and Den.Seed + cleared flags serialise with the world; the den itself is rebuilt from the seed.
connections.godot: No engine code beyond the save menu.
connections.unity: No engine code beyond the save menu.

connections.why: A team enters from the hive's tile and comes back out.
connections.how: CrawlSession holds the party id; the party is 'in crawl' (off the map clock's travel).
connections.godot: Party token shows a 'crawling' badge.
connections.unity: Party token shows a 'crawling' badge.

godot.approach: The den map is a Control drawing rings of chamber arcs in _Draw (polar coordinates: ring = radius, index = angle) or one Polygon2D per chamber for easy clicking. A click on a passage sends a CrawlMove command; each chamber reuses the normal battle scene.

unity.approach: Draw the den map in UI Toolkit with a custom VisualElement using generateVisualContent and Painter2D arcs, or as sprites on a world-space canvas. Load the battle scene additively for each chamber and return to the den map on the result.

learn.t: Red Blob Games: Probability and damage rolls
Red Blob Games: Introduction to A* (BFS, flood fill)

newb: Procedural generation from a seed: save the seed, not the whole den, and the same den comes back every visit.
The crawl is a state machine wrapped around many small battles: keep the between-chamber state (wounds, ammo, known chambers) in one session object.
Show odds by counting dice faces exactly (10 faces of a d10), not by running a simulation.
Test generators with properties ('every mouth reaches the core') over thousands of seeds, not by eyeballing one.
pitfalls: Off-by-one in shown odds (the prototype's issue #63)
Using the world Rng to build dens (it reshuffles the rest of the run)
An unreachable core: validate connectivity in tests
Losing between-chamber state on save/load
test: xUnit: BFS from every mouth reaches the core over 1,000 seeds; every chamber has exactly one wall (rim rules aside); listen odds equal brute-force enumeration; killing the Hivemind destroys the hive; save/load mid-crawl round-trips. Manual: dev-spawn a 2-ring hive and crawl it.

title: Defences: walls, Defenses tab & field works
summary: Everything a base builds to hold: wall pieces (1×1, 1×2, 1×4, gates, stands) in materials by base tier, barricades, sandbags, wire, spike pits, trenches, mines, towers, floodlights and the perimeter alarm, field works outside the walls, and the 'hold' maths that decides if a horde is beaten at the walls.
whyHere: Hordes now reach bases. It needs base map placement, the build queue and the counter-dead read; sieges (100) are fought on the map these pieces make.
subsystems: Defence piece defs & unlocks by base size
Battle cells: wire, spikes, trench, mines, sandbags
sliceScope: Camp tier: barricades plus wood 1×4 wall pieces and a 1×4 gate placed and rotated on the base map; 'Walled' only when a flood fill from the map edge can't get in; hold limit = 15 + 18 × wall strength + 2 per guard combat point; a horde at or under it is beaten off, above it breaks in; a repair order.
fullScope: Camp → shelter → outpost → hub unlocks; materials wood → logs → scrap → metal sheets. Hold 15 + 18 × strength (15/51/87/159/231), multipliers: barricade +12%, trench +25% (second +12%), gate +20%, floodlights +10%, wire +6% a line, concertina +10%, sandbags +5%, towers +8%. Spike pits thin 7% + 4; a minefield 12 mines (2 dead each), two at most; a Wallbreaker cuts to 60%. Repair 1/1.5/2/3 work-hours per 1×4. Alarm 1 power 20:00–06:00. No base gets a wall it did not build.

data: defences.json: piece id, footprint, tab, opens at base size, cost per material, hp per cell, strength, battle cell kind, hold multiplier, artKey
Materials table (wood, logs, scrap, sheets: cost, hp, strength, skill)
Hold constants and multiplier list
Field work kinds (roadblock, well, tower, relay) with cost and hours
backend: Placement validator on the base grid (rotation, no-build margin, overlaps) → PlacePiece command
WallInfo: flood fill from the map edge; a broken piece is a gap
DefenceResolver.HoldCheck(base, attacker) → HoldResult: ONE function for player and group bases (ADR 0001), with counter-dead and tunnel cuts
Consumables: spike pits, mines spent, wire cut; Ring wall planner queues every missing piece
Wall repair order job (broken first, 08:00–20:00); field works as land jobs
Tests for the hold table and flood fill
ui: Defenses tab list with 'Opens at …' locks
Placement ghost (R to rotate, red when invalid)
Hold summary 'Holds ~87 dead' with a breakdown tooltip
'Walled' / 'Not walled: gap at …' indicator

connections.godot: Ghost Sprite2D snapped with LocalToMap/MapToLocal; R rotates; click sends the command.
connections.unity: Ghost GameObject snapped with Grid.WorldToCell; Input System action rotates; click sends the command.

connections.unity: No engine code: sim-to-sim.

godot.approach: Placement happens on the base map's TileMapLayer: a ghost node follows the mouse snapped to cells (LocalToMap / MapToLocal), tinted red when the sim's validator refuses, and a click sends PlacePiece. Use TileSet terrains (autotiling) so sandbags and wall pieces join into continuous walls.

unity.approach: The base map is a Tilemap; a ghost GameObject snaps with GridLayout.WorldToCell and turns on a rotate action. Rule Tiles (2D Tilemap Extras package) give joined sandbags and walls. The sim validates; the ghost only shows the answer.

learn.t: Red Blob Games: Introduction to A* (BFS, flood fill)

newb: The same fight has two resolutions: 'by the numbers' (a formula) and the tactical map. Keep them in line by running the tactical AI on both sides headless and comparing.
Flood fill (BFS) from the map edge is the simplest way to know if a wall is closed: if the fill reaches the yard, there is a gap.
Keep multipliers as a data list, not code: tuning becomes editing JSON.
Autotiling: the engine picks the right sprite (corner, T, straight) from the neighbours, so art can be drawn once per joint.
pitfalls: Free walls for a base type (the prototype removed them)
The hold formula drifting away from real battle outcomes
Flood fill treating diagonals differently from battle pathing (leaks)
Engine-side placement checks that disagree with the sim's
test: xUnit: a closed ring is Walled, one broken piece is not; hold values match the table (15/51/87/159/231); a Wallbreaker cuts to 60%; mines are spent 2 dead each; repair hours per material. Manual: place a ring at a camp, see 'Walled', dev-spawn a horde of 40 and 120.

title: Raids & sieges on the base map
summary: When attackers come for a base (the dead through the walls, raiders, outsiders, a group freeing its people) the fight is played on the base's own map: a deploy step with drilled defence plans, wall → yard → last-stand tiers, siege kit (ladders, rams, grenades), thieves at the real containers and the locked Armory, plus the watch roster, the alarm and attacks on camps.
whyHere: Needs the defences (99), the base map and the tactical systems. Raiders and hordes come first; AI group raids plug in at groups.factions (102) through the same entry point.
sliceScope: One base map type (yard with or without a ring wall); attackers enter from the side they came from; defenders placed by hand; fight until the attackers flee or the base is overrun; wear and losses afterwards; an hourly camp-attack roll from the tile's dead.
fullScope: Wall map 18 × 13+ or the fort map (margin, 4 gates, walkway, towers) then yard and buildings. Breaches pre-cut (+1 at 120 and 250 dead, +1 per Wallbreaker, max 4). Ladders (push-off 15–80%), rams (16–24 a carrier, gate 100–180 hp), grenades over walls, rocks from the walkway. Raids sized 0.6–1.0 × your defence × escalation (+25% per raid repelled, up to 2×), 8 hours at the walls. Defence plans tagged who/when (Default, Horde, Night). Camp grounds attack ~every 30 h when full; the tile trickle by fill³.

data: Siege kit items (ladder, ram, frag grenade) and raid preparedness by era
Defence plan schema (name, who, when, per-map posts by id or role)
Camp attack constants (grounds, trickle, raiders)
Map layout params (margin, gate width, wall column, guard rows)
backend: AttackSystem hourly: camp attacks with hash dice (seed + tile + hour), raid arrivals, lookouts and surprise (watch, alarm)
BaseBattleBuilder: fort / wall / yard maps from the base's real pieces and buildings, rotated to the attack side
DefencePlan.Pick(who, when) and post assignment (by person, else best for role)

title: Autopilot governor (shared decision AI)
summary: One decision AI, a utility-scoring planner, that runs any 'holdout' (a side with bases, people and stores) by issuing the same commands the player's UI sends. It is the player's autopilot, every AI group's brain, and the bot for headless balance runs.
whyHere: It opens the Other-groups milestone because groups.factions (102) needs a brain that plays by the player's rules (ADR 0001 'AI parity'). It also unlocks meta.balance (114) and devtools auto-play; a slim version can be pulled earlier to soak-test the slice.
sliceScope: IController with PlayerController and GovernorController; for one base: each day set roles by need (food, water, wood days), queue the top building wish, launch one scavenging trip to the best known POI, auto-answer cards with their default; Cautious / Balanced / Aggressive weight sets; a console runner plays 1 year and prints a census.
fullScope: The prototype autopilot is ~6,000 lines: roles, building, production, medical, food and defence per base; stewards for safety, supplies, trade, outposts, land and warnings; a 07:00 trip plan; reserves (Cautious); hive campaigns; conquest; power grid wishes. Personalities from Cautious (1 team, range 8, hives from day 150) to Aggressive (3 teams, range 15, hives from day 30). It uses only UI calls, plays on what the player knows and never draws the world's dice.

data: personalities.json: Cautious / Balanced / Aggressive weights (risk, maxTeams, range, reserves, fightBias, hiveFrom…)
Group type profiles (raider, expansionist, zealot, military, fortress, traders, commune) as weight sets for the same considerations
Response curve defs (linear, logistic, step, inverse) by name with parameters
Reserve targets per supply (days of food, water, meds, rounds)
backend: Holdout: every human side, player included; Controller is Player or Governor. Rules are written against Holdout/Base/Survivor and never ask 'is this the player?'

Option generators per domain (roles, builds, crafts, trips, defence, trade, diplomacy) yield candidate commands that already passed CommandBus validation: the governor cannot do what the player cannot
Utility scorer: score = product of consideration curves (0–1) × personality weight; best per domain; a DecisionTrace keeps the top options and reasons
Scheduler: light hourly pass (cards, battles), daily plan at 07:00; distant AI groups run coarser (LOD) but call the same rule functions
Reads a KnowledgeMap (what this holdout has seen/heard), never the true world; uses hash dice or its own Rng stream
Headless runner (console app): N seeds × years, CSV census; swapped-sides parity test and conservation ledger test
ui: Autopilot toggle + personality picker
'Why?' panel: the last decisions with their top-3 scored options
Dev overlay: per-domain option scores for the selected base

learn.t: Game AI Pro (free chapters: utility theory, planners)

newb: Utility AI: list what you could do now, score each option 0–1 on a few considerations ('food days low' through a curve, 'risk' through another), multiply, take the best. It suits economy decisions better than behaviour trees, and personalities are just different weights.
The 'actor' pattern: the player is a holdout whose controller happens to be a human. If a rule contains 'if (isPlayer)', suspect a parity bug.
Going through commands and validation is what guarantees the AI never cheats, and it turns the autopilot into a free test of your command set.
Give the AI the fog the player has: decisions on knowledge, not truth.
Because the sim is engine-free, the governor can play years in seconds: that is how you balance a game this big.
pitfalls: Reading true world state (an omniscient AI the player can feel)
Mutating state directly instead of issuing commands
Drawing from the world Rng, so turning autopilot on changes the world's dice
One giant file: split by domain from day 1 (the prototype's is 6,000 lines)
Full planning every hour for 20 groups: plan daily, react hourly, budget per tick
test: xUnit: each curve; generators yield only commands that validate; same state → same decision; toggling autopilot off leaves state untouched. Integration: headless 1 year × 5 seeds keeps the hub alive above a floor; parity test: swap the player's and a group's controllers and the outcome bands match; conservation ledger shows no goods from nowhere.

title: AI groups: growth, expansion, raids, parity
summary: AI groups (raider gang, expansionist hub, zealots, military remnant, fortress hub, traders, farming commune) are full holdouts: real survivor records, real bases built with the player's construction code, real stock and armory. They grow, expand, build, trip, heal, flee hordes, take over empty bases and raid you and each other, run by the governor with their type's profile.
whyHere: Needs the governor (101) and every player system they must share (survivors, inventory, bases, combat, sieges). Diplomacy, trade, radio, conflict and nomads all hang off it.
sliceScope: 2–3 groups, one Base each, 5–10 members from the Survivor constructor under the group's Rng, starting stock and armory; daily they eat, build through the BuildQueue and scavenge by the trip rules (coarse); goodwill toward you; a hostile type raids your base sized to your defence (0.6–1.0×) through def.sieges; the conservation test passes.
fullScope: 4/7/10/15 groups by world size (up to 24). Type rows: arms 0.6–1.6, raid odds a day (raiders 10.5% after an 8–16 day cooldown), reach 30 tiles; target weight 2.5 × greed × land × grudge × size ÷ (1 + tiles/12); escalation +25% per raid repelled up to 2×. Their works: water, farms, beds, walls, bench, storage and a power grid (solar, batteries, alarm, heaters, charger) on an hourly budget. They learn your bases only by scouting, flee hordes, occupy abandoned bases and keep hidden outposts.

title: Diplomacy, blocs, wars & the Calder Coalition
summary: Relations between every pair of groups (−100..100) and toward you, pacts, AI blocs that ally by type, wars (between groups and on you, with goals, grievances and peace terms), and the Calder Coalition you lead: invitations, a seasonal council, standing with fading modifiers, asks, refusal fatigue and the alliance victory at over half the land.
whyHere: Needs groups (102). Trade, radio and envoys (104, 105) carry its offers; conflict (106) carries out its wars.
sliceScope: A relations matrix with resting values by type pair and 2% daily drift toward them; goodwill toward you moved by named events (a raid −12…); pacts at 28+ (5% a day) that break under 10; wars declared by temper and ended when one side wears out; relation bars on the Groups tab.
fullScope: Resting relations by type (raider −44 with all, traders/communes +30 with peaceful groups) minus neighbour friction (1 a tile under 12) ± 8. Events: raid −12, war −30, peace −15. Blocs by type fit (Syndicate, Compact, Covenant). Grievances by reason fading 1% a day, a peace settles 60%. Coalition: invite at goodwill 50+ with a pact and a job done or a council vote; standing = goodwill + named fading modifiers; asks by card (default refuse); leave under 20; alliance victory over 50% of the land, with claims on adjacent tiles.

Every group at war within a year (no restoring force)

title: Trade, caravans & meeting to trade
summary: Barter with groups, nomads and outsiders through one price model (hidden base value × condition × the buyer's need and mood), in one trade window, by team visits, their caravans at your gates, radio deals, routes and meeting points; caravans are real parties with guards that can be robbed.
whyHere: Needs groups' real stock (trade is one of the few legitimate ways goods move under ADR 0001), item condition and valuation, and parties. Radio deals (105) build on it.
sliceScope: A team visits a group's base; the trade window barters the team's inventory against the group's shelf; price = base value × condition × need × attitude; the group never sells below its reserve; items move between real inventories (ledger: Trade).
fullScope: Their caravans: guards 2 + 1 per 12 people (max 5), carry 60 + 15 a guard, stay 24 h; an unfilled radio deal costs 3 goodwill. Meetings: halfway or a picked tile (land, no base, hive or horde), waiting 48 h, no fee. Groups' convoys swap both ways, meeting halfway when far. Food valued by kcal, shelf life and quality; gear by condition and uses left; prices explained ('At war: rifles wanted').

Demand by group type and state (at war, hungry, winter)
Caravan and meeting constants (guards, carry, stay, wait)

Group convoys between groups; a raided caravan goes through the off-screen resolver
Tests: buy-then-sell-back loses value; conservation through trades

title: Radio network, envoys & intel
summary: Radio stations (12 tiles), military sets (24), relays (6) and powered towers (30) form a network that lets you talk and deal with groups at a distance; without a link every message, yours or theirs, goes by envoy, a real person on the road. Others listen in, and intel is what they learn.
whyHere: Needs groups and diplomacy (messages to carry), buildings and power (stations, towers). It gates trade deals (104) and the coalition's reach.
sliceScope: A radio station building (12 tiles), coverage as the union of nodes, CanRadio(a, b) = coverage + 6 reaches their base AND they have a set; otherwise an Envoy party (1+ survivor) walks there, delivers, and walks back with the answer; coverage rings on a map layer.
fullScope: Radios are mid game (year 5 or the Radio Engineering Handbook). Relays must link to a station by a chain and use 1 part every 10 days; +2 range on generator power. Towers: 2 fuel a day for 30 tiles, wrecked in raids, sabotage 3% a day per hostile base within 12 (max 15%). Envoys can be met, robbed or lost. Intel: your traffic kept for days, stations traced, radio discipline, decoys, captured scouts questioned; listening in on group channels.

godot.approach: Mostly sim. The settle card and negotiate dialog are AcceptDialogs with custom buttons (AddButton) built from the sim's option list; the captives list is a Tree with columns. Ownership changes recolour the territory layer through the normal map refresh.

unity.approach: UI Toolkit modal panels for settle and negotiate built from the sim's option list; the captives list is a ListView.

newb: Ownership transfer touches many systems: make it one well-tested function and route every capture, loss and occupation through it.
A prisoner is still the same Survivor record with a status, never a copy: they can be ransomed, rescued or recruited without losing who they are.
Choices with consequences: executing or holding people feeds grievances, which the diplomacy layer turns into wars later.
pitfalls: Duplicating survivors on capture
Dangling references after a base changes hands (party homes, haul orders, watch roster)
AI jails as special code instead of the same jail rules
Ransom that creates goods instead of moving them
test: xUnit: TransferBase keeps stock and clears orders; jail capacity enforced; escape rate over many days near 5%; ransom price formula by attitude; the rescue map's cell opens with the jailer's keys. Manual: assault a weak group's base and capture people.

title: Nomads, visitors, splinter bands & posted jobs
summary: Humans who are not map groups: nomad bands (Drifters, Looters, Survivalists, Preppers) that camp, raid places and move on; outsiders from beyond the border (raiders, merchants, explorers); splinter bands torn off a group by strife; and jobs groups post over the radio or at their gates.
whyHere: Needs groups, trade and the governor; it rounds out the Other-groups milestone with the roaming humans and the quests that make the map feel populated.
subsystems: Band model & band code (carry, food, care, recruit)
sliceScope: Nomad bands only: Drifters and Looters spawn, camp 2–5 days, raid a POI within 3 tiles (taking what is in its containers), move 4–8 tiles; a meeting card (trade / fight / leave); band members are survivor records with real inventories.
fullScope: Bands of 3–10 in four tiers unlocked by era, each with its kit (makeshift, melee, hunting rifles, rifles + plate + a vehicle); a slow respawn holds them at about half the group count; they leave after 1–2 years; never in diplomacy or the coalition. Outsiders: raiders from day 20–26 then every clamp(30 − 0.06 × day, 10, 30) × 0.75–1.25 days, merchants every 10–16, explorers every 6–12. Jobs: 6% a day (traders 8%), 6 under way at most, decline −1, fail −4 goodwill.

data: nomad_tiers.json: pop range, kit table, attitude, era unlock, art keys
Outsider kinds and spawn curves
Strife constants (decay, pressure, split threshold)
Job templates (cull a horde, deliver goods, escort, scout) with rewards and deadlines
backend: Band : Holdout without bases, sharing a BandCode: carry by the team rule, eat and drink from stores, care by the health code, recruit
NomadSystem daily: camp, survey, raid, move, recruit, respawn (own Rng stream)
Visitors: enter on a border tile ≥6 from your bases, route, exit
Splinters: strife builds, split creates a new Group from real members and a share of goods
Jobs: offer → accept → hourly predicate → reward / fail at deadline
ui: Camp markers once seen
Meeting card by tier
Jobs list in the Groups tab

godot.approach: Nothing special on the engine side: camp markers are Sprite2D nodes shown when the player's knowledge says seen, meeting cards are ui.cards dialogs, the Jobs list is an ItemList in the Groups tab.

unity.approach: Camp markers as pooled sprite prefabs toggled by knowledge; meeting cards and the Jobs list in UI Toolkit.

newb: Not everything needs to be a full group: a Band reuses the Holdout pieces (people, inventory, care) and skips bases and diplomacy. Composition beats one giant class.
Spawn curves as data: you'll tune 'how often raiders come' many times.
A posted job is a small quest: a predicate checked each hour plus a deadline and a reward.
pitfalls: Bands with an infinite shelf (their shelf is only what their people can carry)
Outsiders spawning next to your base
Bands drawing the world's Rng
Splits that create or lose people or goods
test: xUnit: camp/move cycle lengths; respawn holds about half the group count over 3 years; a split conserves members and goods; a job fails at its deadline and costs 4 goodwill. Manual: meet a Drifter band and trade.
